source: NCERT Class VII, Social and Political Life II, Polity Ch. 1.

sections.heading: 1. Equality in a Democracy
points: **Equality** is a key value of **democracy** — all persons are equal in **dignity and before the law**.
In India, **every adult** has the **right to vote** — **universal adult franchise** — regardless of caste, religion, gender, wealth or education.
'One person, one vote' expresses political equality.

sections.heading: 2. Equality in the Constitution
points: The Constitution guarantees **equality** as a **Fundamental Right**.

sub: **No discrimination** on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth.
Everyone has **equal access** to public places (shops, wells, roads, etc.).

points: The Constitution also allows **special help** for disadvantaged groups (e.g. reservations) to make equality real.

sections.heading: 3. Recognising Inequality
points: Despite the law, **inequalities persist** — based on **caste, religion, gender, disability and poverty (wealth)**.
**Dignity** — being treated with respect — is central; discrimination denies dignity.
Example (the chapter): the **Civil Rights struggle** and figures like **Rosa Parks / Dr B.R. Ambedkar** show the fight against inequality.

sections.heading: 4. Towards a More Equal Society
points: Government schemes provide **midday meals, education, healthcare** to promote equality of opportunity.
Laws alone are not enough — **attitudes** must change too.
A democracy works best when **all citizens are treated as equals** in practice.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Equality = a core value of democracy; guaranteed as a Fundamental Right.
Universal adult franchise = every adult can vote; 'one person, one vote'.
Constitution: equality before law; no discrimination (religion/race/caste/sex/birthplace); untouchability abolished.
Special provisions (reservations) help disadvantaged groups.
Dignity = being treated with respect; midday meal scheme promotes equality.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Universal adult franchise** = the right of **every adult** to vote, regardless of wealth or education.
The Constitution **abolishes untouchability** and bans discrimination on five grounds.
Equality allows **special provisions** for the disadvantaged — this is not a violation of equality but a way to achieve it.
Legal equality does not automatically end **social/economic** inequality.
